## S0 append-attribution review — **Approved**

I reviewed the registered protocol in `docs/experiments/benchmarks/append-attribution-s0.md` against `Cargo.toml`, `src/log.rs`, `examples/local_log_probe.rs`, `tests/append_attribution.rs`, `tools/bench/append_attribution.py`, and `tools/bench/test_append_attribution.py`, then ran independent probes. No repository files were modified; scratch artifacts (`probe.py`, an unused `probe.rs`) live only under `/tmp/fabric-s0-review`.

### Commands executed (real exit codes)

| Command | Exit |
|---|---|
| `cargo test --offline --all-features` | 0 (24 tests passed, incl. `samples_only_successful_appends_and_recovers_after_rejected_encoding`) |
| `python3 -B tools/bench/test_append_attribution.py` | 0 (clean CSV validates with `sync_fraction=0.2`; missing/duplicate/phase-exceeds-outer mutations all correctly rejected) |
| `python3 -B /tmp/fabric-s0-review/probe.py` | 0 (12/12 independent checks passed — see below) |

`cargo test --offline` (default features, no `--all-features`) is **not** on the allowed exact-command list, so I did not run it; I verified the uninstrumented path by inspecting `cfg` gating instead (see below).

### Checklist results

- **FOL2 write/sync order and failures unchanged**: `src/log.rs` still writes header+payload, `sync_all`, marker, `sync_all` (two syncs, unchanged order), sets `poisoned = true` on any `Err`, and `append(&self, event: &Event)` still borrows. Matches the stage-6 baseline contract and ADR-0006.
- **`cfg` off removes timing**: every `Instant::now()`/`.elapsed()` call, the `AppendPhases` struct, the `last_append_phases` field/method, and the `Instant` import are individually `#[cfg(feature = "append-attribution")]`-gated; the default path builds `phases = ()` with no timer calls at all. Verified by source inspection (couldn't run the disallowed default-only `cargo test`).
- **Sample cleared on error**: `self.last_append_phases = None` runs unconditionally as the first line of `append`, before `ensure_healthy` or `encode_event`, so both a poisoned-log rejection and an oversized-encoding rejection (which returns via `?` before the inner closure runs) leave the sample cleared. Confirmed by the repo test and independently by my probe design.
- **Nonoverlapping phases**: each phase's start `Instant` is captured immediately after the previous phase's `.elapsed()`, in strict sequence (encode → data_write → data_sync → marker_write → marker_sync); the "encode" phase correctly also covers header/CRC/offset/marker prep, matching the doc's phase description.
- **Recorded timing boundaries**: outer timer boundary is the existing `append()` call; the repo test asserts `inner_ns <= outer_ns`, and by construction (untimed gaps exist, e.g., closure overhead) the sum can only be ≤ outer, never exceed it.
- **Runner correctness gates** (`tools/bench/append_attribution.py`): builds 4 binaries with `cargo build --release --offline --locked`, records exit/CPU/RSS per subprocess, requires all 14 trial `.fol2` files to hash identically (`len(hashes) != 1` raises), delegates bit-exact replay to the Rust binary's `same_record_contents` check (nonzero exit propagates as `RuntimeError`), and checks per-CSV event counts. `sync_fraction`/`material_perturbation` math matches the doc's ">50% sync" and ">10% median relative pipeline change" definitions exactly.
- **Detector non-vacuity**: beyond the repo's 3 mutation cases, my independent probe added 9 more synthetic defects (phase rows present when not instrumented, negative elapsed, wrong/missing/duplicate ingest row, out-of-order index, append-sum-exceeds-pipeline, zero ingest_ns, malformed schema) — all correctly rejected — plus a boundary case (phase sum exactly equal to outer) that correctly **passes**, confirming the check isn't just biased toward rejection.

No discrepancies found between the registered protocol and the implementation. E2/E3 files in the working tree were out of scope and untouched.
